title: Density-aware token and type scale overhaul for multilingual UIs
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Multiple product surfaces are showing inconsistent density and visual weight when localizing to non-Latin scripts and when rendering dense analytics tables. Current token set assumes base metrics tuned for English LTR flows and leaves gaps in: (1) fractional spacing for sub-8px gutters, (2) type sizes that align to commonly-used UI fonts in CJK languages, and (3) micro-elevation values that read clearly at small scales and under chart overlays. This creates visual clipping, perceived instability of cards/rows during hover/focus, and noisy chart color accents in dense dashboards.

Goal: Introduce a density-aware token layer that: (a) adds fractional spacing tokens and a density multiplier, (b) expands the type scale with three international-friendly sizes and platform-specific fallbacks, (c) defines micro-elevation/shadow steps for tight rows and embedded charts, and (d) provides a clear migration path with aliased tokens to preserve backwards compatibility for existing UIs. The work should include design spec, token values, migration codemod, test plans, and a staged Console rollout with telemetry to detect regressions in perceived contrast and layout breakages.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec accepted by PM and Engineering (link to spec) and PR merged that updates token JSON and CSS variables
New spacing tokens (S-0.5, S-1, S-1.5, ... density multiplier x0.75 and x1.25) published and covered in token docs
Typographic scale extended with Size-XS-Intl, Size-S-Intl, Size-M-Intl including font-family fallbacks for CJK and Arabic; tested across Chrome/Firefox/Safari on macOS, Windows, Android
Micro-elevation tokens (E-0 micro, E-1 micro, E-2 micro) defined with both light and dark mode variants and validated on compact table rows (32px and 40px heights)
Migration codemod exists and is documented; automated tests show no layout regressions in Console (visual diff baseline) for top 10 customer pages
Telemetry dashboard setup to track token adoption and layout-related errors for two weeks after rollout
decisions: Use density multiplier approach rather than separate dense component variants to reduce combinatorial token explosion
Introduce three new 'Intl' type sizes scoped to localized components rather than changing global base scale
Prefer subtly softer micro-shadows in dark mode to avoid haloing on chart overlays
tradeoffs: Backward compatibility vs simplicity: aliasing old token names preserves existing components but adds maintenance overhead
Performance vs fidelity: fractional spacing values may increase paint complexity on some older browsers, but are necessary for correct glyph wrapping in CJK
Scope: limiting Intl type sizes to components with explicit localization flags reduces risk but means some legacy screens will not immediately benefit
migration_plan: Step 1: Publish token spec and JSON in repo branch 'design/density-intl-tokens'
Step 2: Run codemod to replace raw spacing/size tokens with aliases where safe; create a report of manual review candidates
Step 3: Merge token PR behind feature flag and run visual diff job across Console staging
Step 4: Enable feature flag for 10% of internal traffic, collect telemetry for 7 days, iterate on edge-case fixes
Step 5: Full rollout after sign-off; deprecate legacy token names with 3-month window and migration docs
